title: How do we draw arcs that bulge inwards on a square?
description: A square of side eight centimetres gets four arcs bulging inwards, one on each side. Each compass tip sits outside the square, eight centimetres from both ends of its side.
teaching_notes: One idea: a compass tip placed equally far from both ends of a side draws an arc through both corners, and a radius equal to the side gives a gentle inward curve. Watch for students who put the compass tip on the side itself, which gives a half circle.

source: Construct 6: Square with Curves, Try This (section 8.4)
video_script.why: A learner draws four equal arcs on a square, placing each compass tip equally far from both ends of a side.
video_script.substitution: the same way as the example in your book: a compass tip placed at a chosen point to draw a curve
video_script.anchor: a square of side eight centimetres with an arc bulging inwards on each side
video_script.payoff_line: Each arc dips about one centimetre into the square.

final_answer.value: Open ended. A square of side 8 cm with four equal arcs bulging inward, each of radius 8 cm, each dipping about 1 cm into the square
final_answer.spoken: dips about one centimetre into the square

maths_rules: the compass tip must be equally far from both ends of a side, so the arc passes through both corners
radius 8 cm = the side, so the tip is 8 cm from both ends of the side
the crossing point is about 6.93 cm outside the side, because the square root of 64 minus 16 is about 6.93
the arc dips about 8 cm − 6.93 cm = 1.07 cm, which is about 1 cm, into the square
video_script.design: The square is drawn, a radius of eight centimetres fixes the compass tip outside each side, and the same step is repeated on all four sides.
